records.title: MRMAC: Mixed Reality Multi-user Asymmetric Collaboration
records.text:
Title: MRMAC: Mixed Reality Multi-user Asymmetric Collaboration
Venue: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR 2023)
Authors: Faisal Zaman, Craig Anslow, Andrew Chalmers, Taehyun Rhee
Tags: vr, ar, 360-video, collaboration
We present MRMAC, a Mixed Reality Multi-user Asymmetric Collaboration system that allows remote users to teleport virtually into a real-world collaboration space to communicate and collaborate with local users. Our system enables telepresence for remote users by live-streaming the physical environment of local users using a 360-degree camera while blending 3D virtual assets into the mixed-reality collaboration space. Our novel client-server architecture enables asymmetric collaboration for multiple AR and VR users and incorporates avatars, view controls, as well as synchronized low-latency audio, video, and asset streaming. We evaluated our implementation with two baseline conditions: conventional 2D and standard 360-degree videoconferencing. Results show that MRMAC outperformed both baselines in inducing a sense of presence, improving task performance, usability, and overall user preference, demonstrating its potential for immersive multi-user telecollaboration.

extras.journal: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality (ISMAR 2023)

records.title: Real-time Stage Modelling and Visual Effects for Live Performances.
records.text:
Title: Real-time Stage Modelling and Visual Effects for Live Performances.
Venue: ACM SIGGRAPH Real-Time Live! (SIGGRAPH 2023)
Award: Audience Choice Award
Authors: Taehyun Rhee, Andrew Chalmers, Faisal Zaman, Anna Stangnes, Vic Roberts
Tags: live visual effects, real-time performance, mixed reality, televerse
We present a novel live platform enhancing stage performances with real-time visual effects. Our demo showcases real-time 3D modeling, rendering and blending of assets, and interaction between real and virtual performers. We demonstrate our platform's capabilities with a mixed reality performance featuring virtual and real actors engaged with in-person audiences.
Press coverage: Step Into the Virtual Arena With Real-time Stage Modeling and Visual Effects; CMIC wins Audience Choice Award at Real-Time Live! SIGGRAPH 2023; University project wins award at international computer graphics conference

records.title: XRGait: Immersive Gait Training Visualization with Integrated Sensing Technology
records.text:
Title: XRGait: Immersive Gait Training Visualization with Integrated Sensing Technology
Venue: 37th Australian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI 2025, ACM SIGCHI)
Authors: Faisal Zaman, Nadia Pantidi, Jacob Young, Rafael K. dos Anjos, Tom Trengrove, James Drown, Jonathan Lee
Tags: gait training, wearable sensors, virtual reality
Gait training and rehabilitation have traditionally been done through movement observation during in-person sessions with medical professionals and follow-up exercises at home. However, these methods are costly, have low patient adherence, and have a decreased accuracy in assessing and modeling patient gait. We present XRGait, a system that seamlessly integrates wearable sensors with immersive technologies to provide real-time support for gait training and rehabilitation. Our system combines smart insoles and wearable motion tracking sensors with immersive displays to provide the patient with real-time feedback about their gait within an engaging training environment. We conducted two studies comparing different system environments and gait visualizations to assess usability and user experience. Findings indicate users found the virtual reality environment most engaging (vs. augmented reality or screen-only) and valued real-time feedback, with a preference for full lower body visualization. We discuss these results, along with limitations and future directions.

extras.journal: 37th Australian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI 2025, ACM SIGCHI)
